title: Successor step of the well-ordered union projective resolution argument
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and n a natural number. Assume that for every R-module N in universe v and every exhaustive monotone well-ordered filtration indexed in universe w, bounds n on the successive quotient projective resolutions imply a bound n on the resolution of N [def-weil-pbc-finite-global-dimension]. Let M have such a filtration F whose successive quotients instead have bounds n+1. Then M has a projective resolution of length at most n+1.

proof.text: For each successive quotient Q e choose the degree-zero projective presentation in its supplied resolution, using zero for zero Q e. Lift each presentation through F e → Q e by categorical projectivity. Sum the lifts into pi : P → M. Induction on e shows each partial sum maps onto F e. Distinct nonzero Q e admit distinct chosen elements of M, so active indices inject into M and the sum can be shrunk into universe v. Componentwise lifting proves P categorical-projective.

Filter K = ker pi by intersections G e with partial sums of P. Finite supports give exhaustion and identify predecessor sums with their union. The predecessor sum maps onto the predecessor union U e in M. The kernel sequence on successive quotients is therefore 0 → G e/G_{<e} → P e → Q e → 0. To prove middle exactness subtract a lift in the predecessor sum of the image of the chosen representative.

Dimension shift this projective presentation to bound the resolution of G e/G_{<e} by n, by the Schanuel proof of Stacks 065S (1). Use the supplied resolution of Q e, not a newly chosen arbitrary projective cover. The existing Lean SES-kernel lemma is restricted to module universe max u v; at unrestricted v the same proof must be formalized categorically. Apply the supplied induction hypothesis to K and G.

Append P → M to the shifted kernel resolution. The image at P is ker pi; injectivity of K → P preserves exactness at the preceding term. All subsequent terms and differentials are unchanged and all terms in degrees above n+1 are zero. For n=0 this is the two-term resolution.

theorem hasProjectiveResolutionLE_of_wellOrderedUnion_succ
    {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (n : ℕ)
    (hIH : ∀ (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) {E : Type w} [LinearOrder E]
      [IsWellOrder E (· < ·)] (F : E → Submodule R M) (hF : Monotone F)
      (hcover : ∀ x : M, ∃ e : E, x ∈ F e)
      (hquot : ∀ e : E, HasProjectiveResolutionLE
        (ModuleCat.of R ((F e) ⧸
          ((⨆ e' : {i : E // i < e}, F e'.val).comap (F e).subtype))) n),
      HasProjectiveResolutionLE M n)
    (M : ModuleCat.{v} R) {E : Type w} [LinearOrder E]
    [IsWellOrder E (· < ·)] (F : E → Submodule R M) (hF : Monotone F)
    (hcover : ∀ x : M, ∃ e : E, x ∈ F e)
    (hquot : ∀ e : E, HasProjectiveResolutionLE
      (ModuleCat.of R ((F e) ⧸
        ((⨆ e' : {i : E // i < e}, F e'.val).comap (F e).subtype))) (n + 1)) :
    HasProjectiveResolutionLE M (n + 1)
